summary: Wabash Valley Power Association asks FERC to correct the E-8 order by removing it from the caption and listing it with the non-jurisdictional transmission owners in footnote 11, because it ceased to be a public utility on January 1, 2025.
ask: Issue an errata removing Wabash from the caption and adding it to footnote 11, or alternatively rescind the show cause order as to Wabash.

points.point: Wabash says it does not dispute the need to address large and co-located load service.
points.quote: WVPA desires to clarify that it does not dispute the need for the Commission to address issues surrounding service to large load and co-located load

points.point: Wabash says it left public utility status on January 1, 2025, as an entity owned by exempt cooperatives.
points.quote: it ceased to be a public utility on January 1, 2025 because it became exempt from the Federal Power Act

points.point: Wabash says it is similarly situated to the non-jurisdictional owners listed in footnote 11.
points.quote: WVPA is a PTO within MISO, however, it is a PTO that is similarly situated to all of the other non-jurisdictional entities listed in footnote 11 of the Order.

points.point: Wabash cites FERC's treatment of a similar ISO-NE request and its CAISO rescission precedent.
points.quote: an errata to the Order would be consistent with the Commission’s treatment of a request from a similarly situated non-jurisdictional entity in Docket No. EL26-72-000

points.point: Wabash asks for the two corrections and, alternatively, rescission as to Wabash.
points.quote: removes WVPA from the caption of Docket No. EL26-70-000, which intended to identify only MISO and jurisdictional PTOs; and (2) adds WVPA in the list of non-jurisdictional PTO entities in footnote 11.

throughLine.text: Seeks correction of who is a named respondent to the E-8 show cause order; FERC granted it in the August 13, 2026 errata notice.
